questions.q: What real-world problem does this lesson's example actually address?
options: How to mine Bitcoin more efficiently
People who can't afford traditional health insurance or fall through the cracks
How to speed up NFT trading
How to build a new cryptocurrency exchange
questions.explain: A student asked how blockchain could replace insurance for people priced out of or overlooked by the traditional system — a genuine non-crypto use case.

questions.q: What warning does this lesson give about applying blockchain to a new industry?
options: Healthcare specifically can never use blockchain technology
Every industry needs its own separate cryptocurrency
Don't just take the idea of Bitcoin and port it directly onto the new industry — design a system suited to the actual problem
Blockchain should never be used outside of cryptocurrency
questions.explain: The instructor explicitly warns against just copying Bitcoin's model — the point is designing around the industry's real problem using blockchain's underlying properties.

questions.q: How do smart contracts remove the need for an insurance company middleman in this proposal?
options: They have nothing to do with payments
They manually process paperwork faster than a human
They automatically release payment when conditions like a diagnosis or treatment record are met
They replace doctors entirely
questions.explain: A smart contract can verify a condition (like a diagnosis) and instantly release funds, without a company deciding whether to approve or delay the payout.

questions.q: What is a "tokenized mutual aid pool" in this proposal?
options: A government-run insurance program
A single wealthy donor funding all healthcare costs
A type of NFT collection
A shared pool people contribute tokens to regularly, which automatically pays out when a member needs care
questions.explain: It works like a digital co-op — contributions accumulate in a shared pool, and the system pays out automatically when someone in the pool needs it.

questions.q: Which Chapter 1 concept makes this healthcare system auditable, per the lesson?
options: The genesis block
Mining difficulty
Transparency and immutability — all actions are transparent and can't be secretly altered
Wallet encryption alone
questions.explain: Because the ledger is transparent and immutable, every action in the system — payments, diagnoses triggering coverage — stays auditable by design.
